This file is the evidence that the Python port is faithful; it is not regenerated from Python, ever. Regenerating it from the code it is supposed to check would turn it into a snapshot of whatever the code does today, which is the opposite of what it is for.

_comment_lifecycle: The five lifecycle verbs -- roadmap-get, roadmap-set-status, roadmap-claim, roadmap-release-claim and roadmap-reconcile -- captured the same way, before their jq was deleted: 149 cases over one adversarial corpus, recording exit code, stdout, stderr, the roadmap.json left on disk, and the whole feature directory listing so a refusal that wrote something as a side effect could not hide. Temp roots normalize to /TMP/<label>; a claimedAt this run wrote is FROZEN while fixture timestamps are dated 2020 and survive verbatim, so an untouched claim stays distinguishable from a rewritten one; the two pids are <LIVEPID> (a process alive for the whole run) and <DEADPID> (one that had already exited). 736 of 745 field comparisons identical after the port -- every stdout, every written file and every directory listing matched in all 149 cases. The nine that differ are stderr and two exit codes, every one of them from jq aborting mid-expression, and they are named here so nobody has to rediscover them. (1) get-next-tasks-sem-userstories, cl-tasks-sem-userstories, re-tasks-sem-userstories, ss-sem-chave-phases and re-sem-chave-phases: jq printed 'Cannot iterate over null' and the bash carried on with the empty capture. The Python reaches the same answer without the engine line. re-tasks-sem-userstories is the one that shows what the empty capture COSTS: reconcile compares "" against the stored status, finds them different, and writes status: "" into roadmap.json. ground_truth() reproduces that on purpose -- it is a defect, and a port is not where a defect is fixed. (2) get-next-sem-chave-phases (exit 5 -> 1) and cl-sem-chave-phases (exit 3 -> 4): a roadmap.json carrying no phases key at all. jq aborted before the verb's own diagnostic could run, so the exit status was the engine's and the message the code was written to print was unreachable; the Python prints it. Both remain refusals that write nothing, which the file and tree fields confirm. Recorded rather than reproduced: synthesizing an engine error would be the only way to match, and that is not a thing to write on purpose. Same shape as dependson-nao-array in the init capture.
